subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Bangladesh Bank Heist
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Bangladesh Bank Heist.

hook.text: Hackers tried to steal $1 billion from Bangladesh's central bank using the SWIFT banking network.

buildup.text: Attackers infiltrated the bank's systems and sent fraudulent transfer requests to the Federal Reserve.

discovery.text: A spelling error in one transfer request flagged the fraud. But $81 million had already been sent.

twist.text: The stolen money was routed through casinos in the Philippines and largely disappeared.

climax.text: A typo saved $900 million. But the $81 million that slipped through showed how fragile banking systems are.

punchline.text: A typo stopped a billion-dollar theft. Barely.

quiz.question: What prevented the hackers from stealing the full $1 billion?
options: A spelling error in a transfer request flagged the fraud
Advanced AI security detected the intrusion
The bank's daily transfer limit was reached
